summary: Cold read of the plan draft: nine blocking handover gaps, and the theme was that the plan described a design without making it EXECUTABLE. Attestation had no envelope, claims, key, TTL or user binding, and the statement route does not even receive a session id - so C14's expiry and other-user refusals could not have been built. C7 had no data source at all, because statement nodes carry no per-line mapping metadata and an opaque token cannot hand a browser what it does not contain. The raw-read seam this capability depends on throws HTTP exceptions and is not exported to ChatModule, so task 2 would have duplicated the sensitive query or lost its typed outcomes to the global filter. The read also found that '/ask isolation' as written was a rendering branch, while the shared provider feeds successful turns into the next request's priorTurns - a grounded explanation would have leaked into an ungrounded request's context. And it caught the verification plan both self-contradicting (fixture-owned classification needs no Bedrock) and able to false-green, because backend hermetic tests run from an allow-list. The one finding that was not mine to fix went to the human: the shipped drill panel already contradicts decision 0025 by hiding a replaced batch's lines, so 'the same line cannot behave two ways' was already false. They chose to have the assistant follow 0025 and ledger the panel's divergence as D-0051 rather than edit a shipped surface.
gaps: Attestation was not an executable design. The statement route and service receive no session id and configuration carries neither a grounding secret nor a TTL, and the plan named no envelope, claims, canonical encoding, key rotation, expiry or user-versus-session binding - so C2 and C14's tamper, expiry and other-user refusals could be neither implemented nor proven.

The request contract was ambiguous: it never said which values are SIGNED versus sent as untrusted copies for mismatch checks - department, function, pins, node and block - nor whether 'no focus' is a local message or an attested request returning C12a's focus-required variant. The chat schema is .strict() and accepts neither shape.

C7 had no data source. Statement nodes do not carry the per-line approved mapping metadata it requires - that lives server-side in the mapping master - and an opaque context cannot supply it to a browser projection. The aggregate variant also risked becoming a new server projection, which decision 0024 forbids.

The raw-read seam was missing. MisDrillService has the pin validation, pre-query audit and predicate this needs, but it is controller-oriented: it throws HTTP exceptions and is not available to ChatModule, so task 2 would have either duplicated the sensitive query or lost the typed replaced/gone/audit-failure outcomes to the global error filter. The assistant's 20-row limit versus the drill's 100-row page was also undefined.

'The same pinned line must not behave two ways' was already false in the shipped product: MisDrillService reads a replaced-but-present batch per decision 0025, but the drill panel HIDES those lines and tells the user to regenerate. The plan promised an assistant that reads and reports replacement without deciding whether to align the panel or deliberately differ.

'/ask isolation' was written as a rendering branch, but both panels share one AskProvider: every turn renders from it AND successful turns feed the next request's priorTurns, so a grounded explanation would have leaked into an ungrounded request's context. The frontend stream request types also do not admit grounding.

Criterion and surface ownership was incomplete: task 3 owned C8 although a crafted Budget focus needs a BACKEND refusal, no task owned rendering the leaf/replaced/gone/not-loaded outcomes, tasks 1 and 2 did not own C14's backend proof matrix, the changed Docs surface had no owner, and the claim that the spec and decision 0038 'land with this story' was stale - both are already committed, and 0038's front matter names ask-reopen-saved-report.

The verification plan could false-green, and contradicted itself. Backend hermetic tests run from an explicit ALLOW-LIST in backend/package.json, so a new test file does not execute until it is listed - a leaf that is not named simply never runs. The plan also demanded LLM_PROVIDER=bedrock while specifying fixture-owned deterministic intent classification, which needs no model at all.

Decision reconciliation was asserted rather than performed: listing 33 decisions in front matter does not state each one's consequence, and decision 0019 in particular requires typed request/response contracts and Swagger documentation for the changed chat and statement surfaces, which the plan never assigned across the buffered and streamed chat paths.
resolutions: RESOLVED in the plan's 'Attestation - the executable design': a base64url canonical-JSON claim set signed with HMAC-SHA256, claims covering scope, an OUTLINE DIGEST rather than the outline, pin ids and sources, master version, user id and exp; bound to the USER id because the statement route has no session id and a session binding would die on refresh; a required config secret whose absence is a startup failure rather than a silently unsigned token; a TTL defaulting to 30 minutes; and an ordered key list so rotation does not invalidate live statements. Task 1 owns plumbing the user id into the statement service.

RESOLVED in 'What is signed, what is merely sent': signed claims are authority; the client's department and function are verified context sent so a mismatch can be REFUSED rather than substituted; node and block travel unsigned and are validated against the signed outline digest. No focus is a SERVER outcome - the dock sends the attested request and the server returns the typed focus-required variant, so the rule is server-owned and provable by a backend leaf - and only 'no statement at all' is local. Task 1 extends the .strict() schema deliberately.

RESOLVED: task 1 adds an ADDITIVE, READABLE node-metadata projection to the statement response, covered by the same attestation digest, and the aggregate chat variant is an INSTRUCTION ONLY - the browser derives descendants and their values from the statement it already holds, so no new server projection crosses the network per aggregate ask and decision 0024 holds.

RESOLVED: task 2 EXTRACTS a domain seam returning typed ok/replaced/gone/audit-failed outcomes instead of throwing, called by both the drill controller and the assistant, with the row limit as an argument - the assistant asks for 20 and the panel keeps its 100.

RESOLVED by the human: the assistant follows decision 0025 and reports the figures while saying plainly that the batch was replaced; the shipped panel is left untouched and its divergence is ledgered as D-0051 with a trigger. The plan's risk section now states the divergence as deliberate and temporary rather than claiming a consistency that does not exist.

RESOLVED: isolation is TURN OWNERSHIP. Task 3 tags each turn with its origin and partitions grounded turns out of both /ask's rendering and the priorTurns /ask sends, and extends the frontend request types on the buffered and streamed paths. C14 requires a leaf on both halves.

RESOLVED: C8's refusal moves to task 2 as a backend rule with its surface half in task 3; task 3 explicitly owns rendering every outcome variant; tasks 1 and 2 each own C14's backend proof for their own criteria; the Docs surface is restated as Unchanged by design because both artifacts are already committed; and task 1 corrects 0038's stories field.

RESOLVED: every hermetic leaf uses a deterministic classifier and a fake provider, and Bedrock appears only in the LIVE CHECK as separate manual evidence. Each backend task must add its new test files to backend/package.json's hermetic list and name real gated leaves, and the plan's risk section records that an unlisted leaf goes green having asserted nothing.

RESOLVED by a 'Typed contracts (decision 0019)' section that assigns the work: task 1 owns the Zod schema and OpenAPI for the extended chat request and the statement response's new fields; task 2 owns the response union's schema and documentation across BOTH the buffered and streamed chat routes, which are separate and must not drift.

rounds.question: Decision 0025 says a replaced-but-still-present batch should be READ and reported. The drill service does that — but the shipped drill panel then HIDES the lines and tells the user to regenerate. So my rule that the same line can't behave two ways is already broken today. What should the assistant do?
options: Assistant reports it; ledger the panel's divergence (Recommended)
Assistant hides it too, matching the panel
rounds.chosen: Assistant reports it; ledger the panel's divergence (Recommended)
